commands.update: Check and install a newer release from the configured channel in this supported installation.
commands.update status: Read policy and installation status without network access.
commands.update enable: Enable automatic updates for this product.
commands.update disable: Disable automatic updates for this product.
commands.--json: Return one structured result on stdout; diagnostics use stderr.

environment.HRANESS_NO_UPDATE: 1 disables incidental checking and installation, including after re-entry.
environment.CI: A true CI marker disables incidental checking and installation.

startup: Run only at the real executable boundary, before application work; importing the SDK does nothing.
Help, version, completion and the update command do not trigger a second incidental check.
Preserve explicit product offline, nested invocation, deployment and exact-version-binding policies.
A supported installation uses active-command leases and an exclusive update lock shared by aliases. Check leases again under the lock before replacing code.
A successful automatic update re-enters the same verified installation once with original arguments and stdin before product work. It never replays completed work.

A valid native receipt whose executable bytes drifted is repairable: explicit `update` reinstalls a verified release under any policy, and automatic-policy startups repair and re-enter before product work. The drifted image never runs product work; repair failure or a non-automatic policy fails closed.
Metadata/offline failures leave an ordinary command usable. An uncertain or failed code replacement must not execute mixed installed code.
Do not kill, restart, or reconfigure another process, service, job, or product database.
installation: Determine ownership from the running entrypoint and verified global package root or native install receipt, not merely a matching executable on PATH.
Respect the original global manager and exact selected version. Support Bun and npm global installations; other managers get accurate instructions until verified support exists.
Reject project dependencies, transient runner caches, source checkouts, linked development installs, foreign paths, and ambiguous installations.
Native installations require a receipt bound to the actual executable path and digest. Product-owned bundled installers or verified atomic replacement may implement installation.
Preserve native archive verification, platform checks, post-install version checks, rollback, and existing attestation requirements.
No privilege escalation, shell command interpolation, changing trust policy, or silently opting into a different release channel.
release: Products fix the package identity and release authority in code.
Select published semantic versions and compare prereleases correctly. Retain the channel of prerelease-only products through verified release-tag identity.
No implicit downgrade, Git main install, branch movement, or fallback to an unrelated public/private package.
Metadata and artifact URLs are validated against the configured provider; malformed or oversized responses fail closed.

Verify the selected canonical npm archive's SRI and package identity before manager writes; configured scope registries cannot substitute root-package bytes. Preserve the manager's transitive-dependency and lifecycle policies.
GitHub and native archive flows verify the product's published digest and stronger existing requirements.
state: Persist updater policy and check cadence in a dedicated user-owned preference directory; bind concurrency records to the actual native executable or owned package-manager global root, independent of preference overrides.
Keep verified package archives and package installation records beside the owned package-manager global root.
Retained verified archives are package-manager dependency sources, not disposable caches. Do not remove an archive while an installation references it.
Refuse foreign or symlinked state paths. Write atomically and validate sizes and owners.
Do not store provider credentials, product data, command input, or sensitive environment values.
A saved disabled or notify policy remains authoritative when a newer default becomes automatic.
